title: Black Friday Live: Stream Deals from $0.99 on Paramount+, Apple TV, Peacock, Prime & More!
body:
The holiday shopping season has arrived early for streaming fans, as a wave of limited‑time offers is slashing the cost of premium video services across the United States. Starting today, consumers can add major platforms such as Paramount+, Apple TV+, Peacock, and a suite of Prime Video add‑ons for as little as $0.99 per month, while a standalone Starz subscription drops to $2.99. The promotions, which run through the weekend and are expected to expire before the end of Black Friday, represent the most aggressive price cuts of the year and could reshape subscription habits ahead of the 2026 holiday binge‑watching surge.

The most eye‑catching deal comes from Amazon’s Prime Video ecosystem, where users can bundle niche channels like Starz, Showtime, and HBO Max for a combined $2.99 monthly fee—far below the typical $9.99 to $14.99 each would cost individually. This “add‑on” model, first introduced in 2023, is now being leveraged as a loss‑leader to draw new Prime members and retain existing ones who might otherwise drift to competing services. Industry analysts note that the move underscores Amazon’s strategy to position Prime Video as a one‑stop shop for both mainstream and premium content, especially as the company prepares to launch its long‑awaited live‑sports hub later this year.

Paramount+ is also offering a steep discount, with a 12‑month plan priced at $0.99 per month for new subscribers—a 95 percent reduction from its standard $9.99 rate. The offer includes access to the network’s expanding library of original series, sports rights for the NFL and UEFA Champions League, and a growing catalog of classic movies. Marketing executives at Paramount have framed the promotion as a “thank‑you” to families gathering for Thanksgiving, encouraging viewers to stream titles like the newly released family drama “Michael” together. The timing aligns with the network’s push to capitalize on the upcoming holiday season, when streaming traffic historically spikes by more than 30 percent.

Apple’s entry into the Black Friday fray is equally compelling. Apple TV+ is now available for $0.99 a month for the first three months, after which the price returns to the regular $6.99. The deal is bundled with a free trial of Apple Fitness+ and a discounted upgrade to the Apple One family plan, which combines music, games, and cloud storage. By bundling services, Apple aims to deepen its ecosystem lock‑in, a tactic that has paid dividends in past years as users adopt multiple Apple products. Observers suggest that the reduced price may also be a response to growing competition from Disney+ and Netflix, which have both rolled out aggressive price‑matching campaigns this quarter.

Peacock, NBCUniversal’s ad‑supported streaming tier, is offering a “Premium Plus” upgrade for $0.99 per month, granting users ad‑free viewing and early access to new episodes of hit series such as “The Office” and “Yellowstone.” The promotion is limited to new accounts and includes a complimentary month of the network’s sports package, which features live Premier League matches and NFL games. This move is part of Peacock’s broader effort to convert its large free‑tier user base—estimated at 30 million active accounts—into paying subscribers before the year‑end deadline for its contractual obligations with content providers.

While the discounts are undeniably attractive, consumer advocates caution that many of the offers are tied to auto‑renewal clauses and may require users to cancel before a specified date to avoid higher rates. Additionally, the proliferation of short‑term promotions could lead to subscription fatigue, prompting some viewers to consolidate their choices rather than juggle multiple low‑cost add‑ons. Market researchers predict that the net effect will be a modest increase in overall streaming spend, as households add new services but also become more selective about long‑term commitments.

Looking ahead, the aggressive pricing battle is likely to intensify as the industry prepares for the 2027 launch of next‑generation streaming hardware and the anticipated rollout of 8K HDR content. Providers that can successfully convert these Black Friday trial users into loyal, long‑term subscribers will gain a decisive edge in a market that is projected to exceed $150 billion in global revenue by 2028. For now, shoppers have a rare opportunity to test a wide array of premium content at near‑cost, setting the stage for a holiday season defined as much by savvy savings as by binge‑watching marathons.
